name: Boracay
short_description: White-sand beaches and lively nightlife on one of the world's best islands.
content: Boracay is one of the most iconic Philippines tourist destinations, consistently ranked among the best islands in the world. Its crown jewel is White Beach, a 4-kilometer stretch of powdery sand and crystal-clear waters. Beyond lounging on the shore, Boracay offers parasailing, kiteboarding, scuba diving, and sunset sailing on a paraw boat.
travel_tips: Book accommodations early during peak season
Follow local environmental rules on beach access
Try island-hopping to nearby coves
Use tricycles for short trips around the island

name: Palawan (El Nido)
short_description: Limestone cliffs, hidden lagoons, and world-class island hopping.
content: El Nido enchants with towering limestone cliffs and hidden lagoons where you can kayak or swim in emerald waters. Part of Palawan, often called the Last Frontier, El Nido is a crown jewel of Southeast Asian travel with dramatic karst landscapes and clear lagoons.
travel_tips: Join organized Tour A/B/C/D packages for lagoon access
Bring reef-safe sunscreen
Cash is useful in smaller establishments
Allow 3–4 days to explore properly

name: Palawan (Coron)
short_description: Pristine lakes, lagoons, and legendary wreck diving.
content: Coron is world-renowned for stunning lakes, lagoons, and diving spots. Kayangan Lake is often called the cleanest lake in Asia, surrounded by towering limestone cliffs. For divers, WWII shipwrecks rest beneath the sea, transformed into coral-encrusted dive sites.
travel_tips: Pay environmental fees at the tourism office
Book dive shops in advance during peak season
Start island tours early to avoid crowds
Fly into Busuanga Airport then van to Coron town

name: Cebu
short_description: History, canyoneering, and the Queen City of the South.
content: Cebu blends history, urban life, and outdoor adventure. In Cebu City, landmarks like Magellan's Cross and the Basilica Minore del Santo Niño anchor the island's Spanish heritage. For nature lovers, Kawasan Falls in Badian is famous for canyoneering through turquoise waters.
travel_tips: Fly into Mactan–Cebu International Airport
Book canyoneering tours with licensed guides
Combine city heritage walks with south Cebu day trips
Try lechon and dried mangoes

name: Bohol
short_description: Chocolate Hills, tarsiers, and Panglao's white-sand beaches.
content: Bohol is famous for unique natural and cultural treasures. The Chocolate Hills are a surreal landscape of over 1,200 grass-covered mounds. Philippine tarsiers, tiny primates with enormous eyes, are protected in local sanctuaries. Panglao Island offers resorts and diving access to coral reefs.
travel_tips: Rent a motorbike or join countryside tours for hills and churches
Visit tarsiers only at accredited sanctuaries
Fast ferries connect Cebu and Bohol in about 2 hours
Combine hills tour with river lunch cruise

name: Siargao
short_description: Surfing capital with lagoons, islands, and laid-back island life.
content: Known as the Surfing Capital of the Philippines, Siargao draws international surfers to Cloud 9. Beyond waves, Magpupungko Rock Pools and Sugba Lagoon offer swimming and paddleboarding surrounded by mangroves.
best_time_to_visit: August–November for surf; March–May for calm waters
travel_tips: Rent a scooter to explore the island
Reserve boat tours for Sohoton in advance
Respect local surf lineup etiquette
Cash and e-wallets are widely used

name: Baguio
short_description: Cool mountain retreat and Summer Capital of the Philippines.
content: Dubbed the Summer Capital of the Philippines, Baguio is a refreshing mountain retreat with cool climate, pine-covered hills, and vibrant culture. Burnham Park, Strawberry Farm in La Trinidad, and Session Road define the city experience.
best_time_to_visit: February for Panagbenga or March–May for coolest weather
travel_tips: Bring a light jacket even in summer
Try ube jam and local coffee
Weekend traffic can be heavy from Manila
Visit Tam-awan Village for Cordillera art

name: Vigan
short_description: UNESCO heritage city of cobblestone streets and Spanish colonial charm.
content: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, Vigan transports visitors to the Spanish colonial era. Calle Crisologo is lined with centuries-old houses, cobblestone streets, and horse-drawn carriages that glow under warm lantern lights at night.
travel_tips: Stay overnight to see Calle Crisologo lit at night
Try empanada and longganisa at Plaza Burgos
Combine with Pagudpud or Banaue on a north Luzon loop
Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestones

name: Banaue Rice Terraces
short_description: Ancient rice terraces carved into the mountains — a UNESCO wonder.
content: The Banaue Rice Terraces, often called the Eighth Wonder of the World, were carved into the mountains more than 2,000 years ago. The more secluded Batad terraces, shaped like an amphitheater, remain actively farmed by Ifugao communities.
best_time_to_visit: December to May for trekking; harvest season for golden landscapes
travel_tips: Hire a local guide for Batad treks
Overnight buses run from Manila (9–10 hours)
Wear sturdy shoes — trails can be steep and muddy
Respect farming communities and terrace boundaries

name: Chocolate Hills
short_description: Over 1,000 unique dome-shaped hills that turn brown in the dry season.
content: The Chocolate Hills are a geological formation of more than 1,000 grass-covered mounds that turn chocolate-brown during the dry season, creating one of the Philippines' most recognizable landscapes.
travel_tips: Visit early morning for clearer views
Combine with a full Bohol countryside tour
Bring sun protection — the viewpoint is exposed
Pair with Panglao for a beach extension

name: Camiguin
short_description: Volcanic island of hot springs, waterfalls, and the Sunken Cemetery.
content: Dubbed the Island Born of Fire, Camiguin packs volcanoes, hot springs, and the haunting Sunken Cemetery marked by a large cross rising from the sea. White Island sandbar offers panoramic views of Mount Hibok-Hibok.
best_time_to_visit: March–May or October for Lanzones Festival
travel_tips: Rent a multicab or motorbike to circle the island
Check weather before White Island boat trips
Try lanzones in season
Flights or ferries from Cagayan de Oro work well

name: Davao
short_description: Gateway to Mt. Apo, Philippine eagles, and Mindanao's cultural heart.
content: Davao City is the largest city in Mindanao, balancing urban development with natural wonders. It is the gateway to Mount Apo, the country's highest peak, and the Philippine Eagle Center protects the endangered national bird.
best_time_to_visit: March for Araw ng Dabaw or August for Kadayawan Festival
travel_tips: Fly into Davao International Airport
Check travel advisories for mountain treks
Try durian, pomelo, and grilled tuna
Samal Island is a short ferry ride away

name: Sagada
short_description: Cool highland town of caves, waterfalls, and hanging coffins.
content: Sagada is celebrated for cool climate, rich Igorot traditions, and stunning landscapes. The Hanging Coffins of Echo Valley reflect ancient burial practices. Sumaguing Cave and Bomod-ok Falls reward adventurous visitors.
travel_tips: Hire cave guides — required for Sumaguing
Expect cool nights; pack layers
Bus from Baguio takes about 5 hours
Respect sacred burial sites and local customs

name: Mayon Volcano
short_description: Perfect-cone volcano with ATV rides, ruins, and adventure views.
content: Mayon Volcano is renowned for its near-perfect cone shape. Visitors admire its beauty at the Cagsawa Ruins, where church remnants stand as a reminder of the 1814 eruption. ATV rides at the foothills add adventure to the experience.
travel_tips: Fly to Legazpi for the best access
Views depend on weather — allow extra days
Try Bicol Express and laing
Combine with Donsol in whale shark season

name: Cebu (Kawasan Falls)
short_description: Turquoise waterfalls and famous canyoneering adventures.
content: Kawasan Falls is famous for canyoneering through turquoise pools and cascades. The multi-level falls are among Cebu's most photographed natural attractions and pair well with south Cebu coastal trips.
travel_tips: Book canyoneering with accredited operators
Wear secure water shoes
Start early to avoid crowds
Keep electronics in dry bags

name: Intramuros (Manila)
short_description: Historic walled city at the heart of the Philippine capital.
content: The walled city of Intramuros is Manila's heritage centerpiece, where cobblestone streets lead to Fort Santiago and San Agustin Church, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
travel_tips: Walk or bike the walls early morning
Combine with National Museum visits
Watch for cultural performances on weekends
Use ride-hailing apps for Manila traffic

name: Panglao Island
short_description: White-sand beaches and diving gateways near Bohol.
content: Panglao offers resorts, beaches, and diving access to coral reefs, with Alona Beach as the main hub for island-hopping and sunset dining.
travel_tips: Fly into Bohol–Panglao International Airport
Book diving in advance during holidays
Combine with Chocolate Hills day tour
Respect marine protected areas

name: Apo Island
short_description: Marine sanctuary famous for sea turtles and snorkeling.
content: Apo Island is a protected marine sanctuary where sea turtles glide among vibrant coral reefs, accessible by boat from Dumaguete or Dauin.
travel_tips: Pay marine sanctuary fees
Do not touch turtles or corals
Bring snorkel gear or rent on-site
Start boat trips early for calmer seas
